display.purpose: Hero h1 only. The single largest scale step; never duplicated elsewhere on a page.

headline.purpose: Section h2 titles. The 2.4x gap between Display and Headline is load-bearing.

title.purpose: List entry h3 titles within sections (projects, services rows).

body.purpose: All reading copy. Cap at 65-75ch via max-w containers.

label.purpose: JetBrains Mono uppercase overlines, tech stack tags, category markers. Never more than four words.

shadows.name: ultraviolet-bloom
shadows.purpose: The only permitted shadow. Applied on hover to interactive elements (buttons, card containers). Reads as the surface energizing, not floating. Prohibited at rest.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions. Ease-out only — no bounce, no elastic, no spring.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Button and nav hover transitions (color, opacity, border-color).

motion.name: duration-enter
motion.purpose: Framer Motion entrance animations (fade-in + y offset). Stagger children at 0.1s intervals. All durations collapse to 0 when useReducedMotion() returns true.

narrative.overview:
This is a system designed to prove a thesis before the reader finishes the first scroll: D8 builds things that work, without wasted material. Every spacing step is deliberate. Every border is hairline-thin or absent. Every color decision is load-bearing, not decorative. The canvas is near-black because the work commands all attention — ornament has nowhere to hide.

The dominant aesthetic is restraint at the surface, density underneath. Not minimalism as trend, but minimalism as engineering doctrine. PRODUCT.md calls for "simple outside, powerful inside." This system achieves that by making the whitespace earn its place, the typography carry full structural weight, and the one expressive color — Ultraviolet — appear only where it needs to cut through.

The system explicitly rejects startup-palette accents, gradient text, glassmorphism used decoratively, hero-metric templates, identical card grids, bounce animations, and any aesthetic that depends on a trend to function. If the design still works in 2030, it passes.
keyCharacteristics: Single expressive color (Ultraviolet) used sparingly — never decoratively
Sharp 2px corners everywhere — no softness, no warmth at rest
Typography carries all hierarchy; icons and illustration are absent
Flat surfaces at rest; depth through tonal stepping and hairline borders
Interactive hover states use color shift or opacity reduction — no scale, no bounce

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Ultraviolet (#9900ff) is used on 10% or less of any given screen. Its rarity is the mechanism. When it appears, it is the only thing asking for attention. Never introduce a second accent color.

rules.name: The Large-Text Exception
rules.body: #9900ff on #080808 yields 3.62:1 — AA-compliant at 18px bold or 24px regular and above. Below those thresholds, use #b84dff (5.29:1). Never use the base Ultraviolet for body copy or small labels.

rules.name: The Scale Gap Rule
rules.body: Display to Headline is a 2.4x jump (72px to 30px). This gap is load-bearing: it prevents the page from reading as a flat list of equally-weighted headings. Do not introduce intermediate heading sizes that compress this ratio.

rules.name: The Mono Reservation Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for labels, tags, and technical markers. Never use it for body copy or nav links. Its appearance signals: this is a category, a system, a technical datum.

rules.name: The Bloom Rule
rules.body: The only permitted shadow is the Ultraviolet ambient bloom on interactive hover (box-shadow: 0 0 24px rgba(153, 0, 255, 0.15)). Drop shadows, card shadows, and elevation shadows at rest are prohibited. If a surface needs to feel elevated at rest, step the tonal value — never add a shadow.

rules.name: The Blur Rule
rules.body: backdrop-filter: blur is permitted only on the fixed Nav, where it is structural. Blur applied to cards, modals, or decorative overlays is glassmorphism. Prohibited.

dos: Do use #b84dff (Ultraviolet Accessible) for any purple text below 24px, or bold text below 18px.
Do keep Ultraviolet to 10% or less of any given screen surface.
Do use JetBrains Mono for all technical labels, stack tags, and category markers — uppercase, tracking-widest.
Do maintain 2px radius on every interactive element and container.
Do use 1px Hairline borders (#1e1e1e) as dividers — visible only on close inspection.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: set Framer Motion duration to 0 when useReducedMotion() is true.
Do cap body copy at 65-75ch via max-w-2xl or max-w-md containers.
Do step tonal values (Void to Surface) to create depth at rest.
donts: Don't use gears, circuit boards, wrenches, or generic engineering iconography as decoration.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient background).
Don't use glassmorphism decoratively. The Nav's backdrop-blur-sm is structural; blur on cards is prohibited.
Don't use purple-to-blue gradients or mix Ultraviolet with other saturated hues.
Don't add drop shadows, ambient shadows, or glow effects at rest.
Don't use Inter. Space Grotesk for headings, IBM Plex Sans for body.
Don't introduce a second accent color.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing on any animation.
Don't use stock photo heroes or mascot illustrations.
Don't add taglines inside the logo, founding-year callouts, or 'since 2025' anywhere.
Don't use startup palette accents: neon green, saturated yellow, retro pastels.
